evidence_set: General-population sample: NLAES (1991–1992, response 90%) and NESARC (2001–2002, response 81%) pooled; 53,238 US-born adults aged 18–57 in five 10-year birth cohorts (born 1934–1943 to 1974–1983), 4,603 to 16,329 per cohort; people older than 57 and people born outside the US excluded; lifetime drinkers had had more than 12 drinks; ages at first drink, at onset of DSM-IV alcohol dependence (AUDADIS-IV) and at first alcohol treatment were all recalled at one interview.
